newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army kills 10 Tamil rebels in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army kills 10 Tamil rebels in north.

text.p: At least 10 Tamil separatist rebels were killed by Sri Lankan troops as they crossed a shallow lagoon in a bid to infiltrate army defences in the northern Jaffna peninsula, military officials said on Sunday.
The rebels were detected by soldiers as they waded through the Jaffna lagoon heading towards the peninsula shortly after midnight on Friday, the officials said.
"It was a large group of rebels, probably more than a hundred of them," one officer told Reuters.
Soldiers opened fire and the navy, which was called in to assist, also engaged the rebels in a firefight which lasted till dawn. The rebels later retreated towards Pooneryn on the mainland, he said.
On Saturday morning, troops discovered 10 rebel bodies, some of them believed to be those of "Sea Tiger" cadres belonging to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), officials said.
One soldier was killed and two were wounded from rebel fire, they added.
The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, was not available for comment.
The former LTTE stronghold of Jaffna, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo, has been under army control since it was captured from the rebels in early 1996.
The rebels, operating from bases just south of Jaffna, have launched attacks on the peninsula from time to time.

The military is believed to be preparing for a major offensive to open a land route linking Vavuniya, 220 km (140 miles) north of Colombo, with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The military relies on air and sea transport to send troops and supplies to bases in Jaffna because much of the forested region north of Vavuniya is under rebel control.
The government says more than 50,000 have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers say the death toll is higher.
